kind: pre-fix diagnostic (implementation still in progress; reported to Lead)

environment.game: asset-zip-v2 test package installed through POST /api/game-market/install-local

question: Can the platform wrapper (resource origin, static) embed the game document when the Runtime sandbox attribute is applied to the outer wrapper iframe as packages/runtime/src/controller.js does today?

sessions.value: {"href":"chrome-error://chromewebdata/","origin":"null","title":"127.0.0.1","body":"127.0.0.1 拒绝了我们的连接请求。","iframes":0}

network.csp: default-src 'none'; script-src http://127.0.0.1:55028; style-src http://127.0.0.1:55028; img-src http://127.0.0.1:55028

browserLog: Framing 'http://127.0.0.1:55028/' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "frame-ancestors http://127.0.0.1:* http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:55028". The request has been blocked.

finding.summary: With sandbox="allow-scripts" on the outer wrapper iframe (current controller.js), the wrapper document runs with an OPAQUE origin ("null"). The nested game document CSP frame-ancestors lists the resource origin URL and http://127.0.0.1:*, but an opaque-origin ancestor can never match a host-source, so Chrome blocks the nested frame: "Framing 'http://127.0.0.1:<resPort>/' violates ... frame-ancestors http://127.0.0.1:* http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:<resPort>". The game target falls back to chrome-error; no game resources load.
finding.contractConflict: docs/V1.5-CONTRACTS.md §7.5 asset-zip-v2 entry CSP MUST include frame-ancestors <DSH web origin>; §7.5.1 MUST use the platform wrapper; current Runtime MUST sets sandbox="allow-scripts" on its only iframe (never allow-same-origin). These three MUSTs cannot hold simultaneously: the wrapper is an ancestor of the game document; a sandboxed wrapper has an opaque origin and cannot be listed in frame-ancestors.
finding.verifiedControl: Removing only the outer sandbox attribute (wrapper served unchanged, same CSP) makes the same launch load and run: game document title "Orbit Courier", body "ready", stylesheet + script 200, no CSP violation log. So the cause is isolated to the outer sandbox/opaque ancestor, not to the wrapper document or its CSP.
candidateFixes: A (recommended, needs M1-D + contract §7.5.1 update): the Runtime MUST NOT sandbox the platform wrapper iframe (it is static platform content, no game bytes, CSP nonce-pinned relay); the nested GAME iframe keeps sandbox="allow-scripts" and the game document keeps its exact frame-ancestors. Security invariant becomes: game document is sandboxed and opaque; wrapper is trusted platform UI hosted on the resource origin.
B (rejected): remove frame-ancestors from the game CSP, or use * — weakens the contract anti-embedding boundary.
C (rejected): add allow-same-origin to the outer iframe — explicitly forbidden by project/contract rules.
finding.evidenceLimits: Chromium 155 only; the outer iframe in case A is created by this diagnostic exactly like packages/runtime/src/controller.js createIframe() (sandbox="allow-scripts" + allow=autoplay + referrerpolicy=no-referrer). The real controller path is re-tested once M1-D lands a decision.
